## docs(openapi): add /plans endpoints + Plan schema + PlanResetPeriod

Documents the v0.6.0 plans CRUD surface in the panel's
OpenAPI spec. The Go side (#131, #132) and the
hand-mirrored API client (this PR) are now in sync
with the spec.

### What ships in this PR

- `docs/openapi.yaml` — adds:
  - `/plans` (GET, POST) endpoints
  - `/plans/{id}` (GET, PATCH, DELETE) endpoints
  - `Plan` schema (id, name, trafficLimitBytes,
    durationNs, deviceLimit, resetPeriod, priceCents,
    createdAt, updatedAt)
  - `PlanCreateRequest` (name + durationNs required,
    rest optional)
  - `PlanUpdateRequest` (all fields optional,
    PATCH semantics)
  - `PlanListResponse` (wraps the array)
  - `PlanResetPeriod` enum (daily / weekly / monthly /
    never)
  - Info.version bumped 0.2.0 → 0.6.0
  - Info.description updated with the v0.6.0 surface
    list (incl. /backups from #120)
  - The /plans section sits between /hosts and /users
    — the natural ordering in the data graph (hosts →
    plan_pool → plans → users)
- `frontend/src/api/services/plans.ts` — new
  hand-mirrored service. 5 functions (listPlans,
  getPlan, createPlan, updatePlan, deletePlan) +
  CreatePlanRequest / UpdatePlanRequest request
  types. Follows the exact shape of services/users.ts.
- `frontend/src/api/services/index.ts` — adds
  `export * from './plans'`. The alphabetical order is
  kept (auth, nodes, inbounds, hosts, plans,
  subscription, panelcfg, users, audits, backups) —
  plans sits between hosts and subscription, matching
  the data-graph order.
- `frontend/src/types/aegis.ts` — updates the legacy
  `Plan` interface: `durationDays: number` →
  `durationNs: number`. The new wire format is int64
  nanoseconds (the Go side stores it as Postgres
  INTERVAL). The rendering layer (PlansView, planned
  for #134) converts to a human-readable "30 days"
  string. The ResetPeriod type alias already matched
  the new enum and needed no change.
- `frontend/src/types/api.d.ts` — auto-regenerated by
  `npm run codegen`. The new Plan / PlanCreateRequest /
  PlanUpdateRequest / PlanListResponse / PlanResetPeriod
  types appear at lines ~2652-2730. The hand-mirrored
  service file uses the same wire format as the
  generated types, so the `codegen:check` step stays
  green.

### Why durationNs, not durationDays

The Go side (`internal/plans/plan.go`) stores Duration
as `time.Duration` (nanoseconds) and encodes it as
`pgtype.Interval` in Postgres (microsecond precision
on the server, full nanosecond precision in the Go
type). Sending "30 days" as a fixed int would lose
"1 hour" / "30 minutes" plans. The int64 nanoseconds
wire format is the canonical Postgres-INTERVAL-via-pgx
path; the UI converts to a human-readable string at
the rendering layer (the PlansView in #134).

### Pre-existing spec inconsistency (NOT fixed here)

The existing schemas (User, Node, Host, …) use
camelCase keys in the OpenAPI spec while the actual
Go wire format is snake_case (the `camelizeKeys`
response interceptor in `client.ts` bridges the two).
The new Plan schema follows the existing convention
(camelCase) so the type generation is consistent with
the rest of the spec. A full wire-format normalization
across all schemas is a separate work item — the
change is too big for a single PR and would break
every consumer.

### How to verify locally

```sh
cd frontend
npm run codegen       # regenerates api.d.ts from openapi.yaml
npm run codegen:check # must say "codegen up to date"
npm run type-check    # vue-tsc, no errors
npm run lint          # eslint, no errors
npm run build         # vite build, no errors
```
